Quick answer: Tella is the best all-round Loom alternative when you want the finished video to look polished without leaving the tool: screen and camera recording on Windows, Mac, and the web, AI Auto Cut, Auto Zoom, and Auto Layouts, a hosted link with viewer analytics, team workspaces, and a free Loom import tool. Loom still wins for quick, rough internal updates in an Atlassian stack. Pick Screen Studio for cinematic Mac-only exports, Vidyard for sales workflows, Descript for transcript-first editing, Cap for open-source recording, or OBS for free local capture. [...] ### What is the best free Loom alternative?

Tella, Cap, OBS, ShareX, QuickTime, and Screenity can all make sense as free or low-cost Loom alternatives, depending on the job. Pick Tella if you want a hosted recording and editing workflow with a free trial. Pick OBS, ShareX, QuickTime, or Screenity if you mostly want local recording and do not need built-in hosting, analytics, or team collaboration.

### Is Tella better than Loom?

Tella is better than Loom for creators and teams who need more than basic record-and-share. Tella adds AI editing, auto zoom, auto layouts, background music, custom branding, viewer analytics, CTAs, and Loom folder import for your existing library. Loom is still a familiar choice for quick internal updates, especially in companies already using Atlassian tools. [...] ### Loom alternatives for mobile and Chrome

1. Screenity: A free Chrome extension for screen recording with annotations, contextual feedback, and drawing tools. Great for quick browser-based captures.
2. Bubbles: Allows you to collaborate by simply clicking anywhere on the screen. It is as simple as clicking, commenting, and sharing.
3. ScreenApp: A browser recorder that turns meetings and uploaded videos into transcripts, summaries, notes, and other AI-generated outputs.

### Loom alternatives that record internal audio

1. Vidyard: A screen recording platform with the option to record internal audio only.
2. Snagit: Allows you to record your screen as an MP4 video or as a GIF.

## FAQ

Why are people leaving Loom in 2026? Two reasons dominate: the 2026 billing migration that retired the free Creator Lite seat and auto-upgraded those users to paid seats — producing surprise invoices — and performance complaints (lag, sync issues, failed uploads) since Loom moved onto Atlassian’s infrastructure. Loom’s free tier is also capped at 25 videos and 5 minutes each.

What’s the best free Loom alternative? For unlimited recording with no watermark, Kommodo and OBS Studio are the strongest free options. ScreenPal’s free tier allows 15-minute clips (with a watermark), and Vidyard’s free plan is the best free choice for sales teams thanks to viewer analytics. [...] ## 2. Tella

An all-in-one recorder and editor that works on Mac, Windows, and Chrome — the closest thing to a full Loom replacement with better editing built in.

What makes it different from Loom: Tella records screen and camera like Loom but bundles layouts, backgrounds, and click-to-trim editing so you can polish a video without a separate app. Unlike Mac-only tools, it runs cross-platform and in the browser, and it targets creators and founders who want share-ready videos rather than raw captures.

Best for: Creators and founders who want recording plus light editing in one place, on any OS.

Pricing: Pro from about $12/month billed annually; 7-day free trial, no card required.

## 3. ScreenPal [...] ## 1. Screen Studio

The Mac tool that made polished product demos look effortless — automatic zoom-ins, smooth cursor motion, and background blur applied after you record.

What makes it different from Loom: Loom captures a raw talking-head-plus-screen clip; Screen Studio turns a plain recording into something that looks professionally edited without you touching a timeline. Automatic zoom follows your clicks, cursor movement gets smoothed, and you export up to 4K. It’s the go-to for marketing videos, launch clips, and app walkthroughs where production quality matters.

Best for: Mac users making demo and marketing videos that need to look sharp.

Pricing: $9/month billed annually (about $108/year); students get an academic discount. Mac only.

Loom remains a strong choice for fast internal recordings and share links. An alternative becomes useful when the real job is a polished customer demo, transcript-led edit, sales workflow, training library, or a finished video built from more than one source.

We checked Loom's official pricing on August 5, 2026. Starter was $0 with 25 videos and five-minute screen recordings; Business was $18 per user per month with unlimited videos and basic waveform editing; Business + AI was $24 per user per month with additional AI editing and video-to-text features.

The eight options below are organized by use case. The acquisition and Atlassian context matters, but it comes after the practical decision: what should replace Loom for the work your team actually does? [...] Atlassian fit cuts both ways. Loom's Jira and Confluence direction is valuable for teams already deep in Atlassian. Teams outside that stack may prefer tools built around sales outreach, creator polish, training, or AI video generation.

## Quick comparison [...] ### Best for

Pick Descript if you record demos, explainers, podcasts, webinars, or customer interviews and want transcript-first editing.

### Watch-outs

Descript can be more editor than messenger. For fast internal updates, Loom or Tella may feel lighter. For on-brand business-video generation from multiple inputs, ngram is more purpose-built.

## 4. Vidyard

Vidyard is the sales-led Loom alternative. Its current pricing page frames the product around revenue teams, with Free, Starter, Teams, Enterprise, and a Video Agent add-on for AI-personalized workflows. The page calls out CRM and marketing-automation integrations, branded sharing pages, CTAs, password protection, captions, team analytics, and secure playback depending on plan.
